Appendix B • Proofs & Comments

B.4 Curves realizing the vector space operations of \(T_p\mathcal{M}\) (§4.1)

In Section 4.1 we defined the tangent space \(T_p\mathcal{M}\) at a point \(p \in \mathcal{M}\) as the collection of velocity linear maps associated with smooth curves passing through \(p\). The algebraic structure of \(T_p\mathcal{M}\) as a real vector space was introduced by endowing it with the operations of addition and s-multiplication, defined operationally via their action on smooth functions \(f \in C^\infty(\mathcal{M})\): \begin{align*} (v_{\gamma_1, p} \oplus_T v_{\gamma_2, p})(f) &\coloneqq v_{\gamma_1, p}(f) + v_{\gamma_2, p}(f), \\ (\alpha \odot_T v_{\gamma, p})(f) &\coloneqq \alpha \cdot v_{\gamma, p}(f). \end{align*} While these definitions correctly encode the vector space axioms, an important subtlety arises from the fact that each tangent vector is itself defined via the velocity of some smooth curve passing through \(p\). Therefore, to guarantee that \(T_p\mathcal{M}\) is closed under \(\oplus_T\) and \(\odot_T\)—that is, that the result of these operations still corresponds to the velocity of a smooth curve passing through \(p\)—it is necessary to demonstrate that such curves indeed exist. In other words, we must prove the following:

  • For any two smooth curves \(\gamma_1\) and \(\gamma_2\) passing through \(p\), there exists a third smooth curve \(\sigma\) whose velocity satisfies \(v_{\sigma, p} = v_{\gamma_1, p} \oplus_T v_{\gamma_2, p}.\)

  • For any smooth curve \(\gamma\) passing through \(p\) and any real scalar \(\alpha \in \mathbb{R}\), there exists a smooth curve \({\sigma}\) whose velocity satisfies \(v_{{\sigma}, p} = \alpha \odot_T v_{\gamma, p}.\)

This appendix provides a constructive proof of these facts:

  1. To prove the existence of a smooth curve realizing the addition operation \(v_{\gamma_1, p} \oplus_T v_{\gamma_2, p}\) for two tangent vectors \(v_{\gamma_1, p}, v_{\gamma_2, p} \in T_p\mathcal{M}\), we proceed as follows.

    Let \(\gamma_1, \gamma_2 : \mathbb{R} \longrightarrow \mathcal{M}\) be two smooth curves passing through \(p\), i.e., there exist parameters \(\lambda_1, \lambda_2 \in \mathbb{R}\) such that \(\gamma_1(\lambda_1) = \gamma_2(\lambda_2) = p\).

    We construct a new curve \(\sigma_{\mathscr{X}} : \mathbb{R} \longrightarrow \mathcal{M}\), defined in terms of a local chart \(\left(\mathcal{U}, \mathscr{X}\right)\) with \(p \in \mathcal{U}\), as follows: \begin{align} \sigma_{\mathscr{X}}(\lambda) := \mathscr{X}^{-1} \big[ (\mathscr{X} \circ \gamma_1)(\lambda_1 + \lambda) + (\mathscr{X} \circ \gamma_2)(\lambda_2 + \lambda) - (\mathscr{X} \circ \gamma_1)(\lambda_1) \big] =... \tag{B.1}\\ ... = \mathscr{X}^{-1} \big[ (\mathscr{X} \circ \gamma_1 \circ \textrm{\runic ᚱ}_1)(\lambda) + (\mathscr{X} \circ \gamma_2 \circ \textrm{\runic ᚱ}_2)(\lambda) - (\mathscr{X} \circ \gamma_1 \circ \textrm{\runic ᚱ}_\varnothing)(\lambda) \big]=... \tag{B.2}\\ ... = \mathscr{X}^{-1} \big[ \big( (\mathscr{X} \circ \gamma_1 \circ \textrm{\runic ᚱ}_1) + (\mathscr{X} \circ \gamma_2 \circ \textrm{\runic ᚱ}_2) - (\mathscr{X} \circ \gamma_1 \circ \textrm{\runic ᚱ}_\varnothing)\big) \big] (\lambda). \tag{B.3} \end{align} Where we have defined the reparametrization functions \[ \begin{aligned} &\begin{array}{c} \begin{aligned} \textrm{\runic ᚱ}_1 \colon \mathbb{R} &\longrightarrow \mathbb{R} \\ \lambda &\longmapsto \textrm{\runic ᚱ}_1(\lambda) \coloneqq \lambda + \lambda_1 \end{aligned} \end{array} \quad &\begin{array}{c} \begin{aligned} \textrm{\runic ᚱ}_2 \colon \mathbb{R} &\longrightarrow \mathbb{R} \\ \lambda &\longmapsto \textrm{\runic ᚱ}_2(\lambda) \coloneqq \lambda + \lambda_2 \end{aligned} \end{array} \quad &\begin{array}{c} \begin{aligned} \textrm{\runic ᚱ}_\varnothing \colon \mathbb{R} &\longrightarrow \mathbb{R} \\ \lambda &\longmapsto \textrm{\runic ᚱ}_\varnothing(\lambda) \coloneqq \lambda_1 \end{aligned} \end{array} \end{aligned} \] This construction corresponds, in local coordinates, to performing a vector addition of the coordinate representations of the curves’ increments around the point \(p\). It is immediate to verify that \(\sigma(0) = p\).

    Now applying the multidimensional chain rule (check the footnote in subsection 4.1.1) forwards and then backwards: \begin{align*} v_{\sigma_{\mathscr{X}}, p}(f) &:= (f \circ \sigma_{\mathscr{X}})'(0) = \left( f \circ (\mathscr{X}^{-1} \circ \mathscr{X}) \circ \sigma_{\mathscr{X}} \right)'(0) = \left( (f \circ \mathscr{X}^{-1}) \circ (\mathscr{X} \circ \sigma_{\mathscr{X}}) \right)'(0) \\ &= \sum_{i} \left\lbrace \left[ (\mathscr{X} \circ \sigma_{\mathscr{X}})_i \right]'(0) \cdot \partial_i (f \circ \mathscr{X}^{-1}) \big( \mathscr{X}(p) \big) \right\rbrace \\ &= \sum_{i} \left\lbrace \left[ (\mathscr{X} \circ \gamma_1 \circ \textrm{\runic ᚱ}_1)_i'(0) + (\mathscr{X} \circ \gamma_2 \circ \textrm{\runic ᚱ}_2)_i'(0) - (\mathscr{X} \circ \gamma_1 \circ \textrm{\runic ᚱ}_\varnothing)_i'(0) \right] \cdot \partial_i (f \circ \mathscr{X}^{-1}) \big( \mathscr{X}(p) \big) \right\rbrace \\ &= \sum_{i} \left\lbrace \left[ (\mathscr{X} \circ \gamma_1)_i'(\lambda_1) + (\mathscr{X} \circ \gamma_2)_i'(\lambda_2) \right] \cdot \partial_i (f \circ \mathscr{X}^{-1}) \big( \mathscr{X}(p) \big) \right\rbrace \\ &= \sum_{i} \left\lbrace (\mathscr{X} \circ \gamma_1)_i'(\lambda_1) \cdot \partial_i (f \circ \mathscr{X}^{-1}) \big( \mathscr{X}(p) \big) + (\mathscr{X} \circ \gamma_2)_i'(\lambda_2) \cdot \partial_i (f \circ \mathscr{X}^{-1}) \big( \mathscr{X}(p) \big) \right\rbrace \\ &= \left( (f \circ \mathscr{X}^{-1}) \circ (\mathscr{X} \circ \gamma_1) \right)'(\lambda_1) + \left( (f \circ \mathscr{X}^{-1}) \circ (\mathscr{X} \circ \gamma_2) \right)'(\lambda_2) \\ &= \left( f \circ (\mathscr{X}^{-1} \circ \mathscr{X}) \circ \gamma_1 \right)'(\lambda_1) + \left( f \circ (\mathscr{X}^{-1} \circ \mathscr{X}) \circ \gamma_2 \right)'(\lambda_2) \\ &= (f \circ \gamma_1)'(\lambda_1) + (f \circ \gamma_2)'(\lambda_2) \\ &= v_{\gamma_1, p}(f) + v_{\gamma_2, p}(f). \end{align*} which confirms that the curve \(\sigma\) realizes the tangent vector \(v_{\gamma_1, p} \oplus_T v_{\gamma_2, p}\) according to the operational definition of addition in the tangent space \(T_p\mathcal{M}\).

    As anticipated, while the construction was carried out using a local chart, the resulting tangent vector is independent of the chosen chart, since the final expression for the velocity depends only on derivatives evaluated at \(p\), which transform covariantly under chart transitions.

  2. To prove the existence of a smooth curve realizing the scalar multiplication operation \(\alpha \odot_T v_{\gamma, p}\) for a given tangent vector \(v_{\gamma, p} \in T_p\mathcal{M}\) and scalar \(\alpha \in \mathbb{R}\), we proceed as follows.

    Let \(\gamma : \mathbb{R} \longrightarrow \mathcal{M}\) be any smooth curve passing through \(p\), i.e., such that \(\exists \lambda_1 \in \mathbb{R}\) with \(\gamma(\lambda_1) = p\). We construct the reparametrized curve \({\sigma} : \mathbb{R} \longrightarrow \mathcal{M}\) as: \begin{align*} {\sigma}(\lambda) \coloneqq \gamma\big(\textrm{\runic ᚱ}_\alpha(\lambda)\big) = (\gamma \circ \textrm{\runic ᚱ}_\alpha)(\lambda), \end{align*} where the reparametrization function \(\textrm{\runic ᚱ}_\alpha\) is defined by: \begin{align*} \textrm{\runic ᚱ}_\alpha : \mathbb{R} &\longrightarrow \mathbb{R} \\ \lambda &\longmapsto \textrm{\runic ᚱ}_\alpha(\lambda) \coloneqq \alpha\lambda + \lambda_1. \end{align*} It is immediate to verify that \({\sigma}(0) = \gamma(\lambda_1) = p\), so \({\sigma}\) is indeed a curve passing through \(p\).

    Now, applying the chain rule for the composition of smooth functions, we compute the velocity of \({\sigma}\) at \(p\) with respect to any smooth function \(f \in C^\infty(\mathcal{M})\): \begin{align*} v_{\sigma, p}(f) &\coloneqq (f \circ {\sigma})'(0) = \frac{d}{d\lambda}\Big|_{\lambda=0} (f \circ \gamma \circ \textrm{\runic ᚱ}_\alpha)(\lambda) = ...\\ ...& = \textrm{\runic ᚱ}_\alpha'(0) \cdot (f \circ \gamma)'(\textrm{\runic ᚱ}_\alpha(0)) = \alpha \cdot (f \circ \gamma)'(\lambda_1) = \alpha \cdot v_{\gamma, p}(f). \end{align*} This shows that the curve \({\sigma}\) realizes the scalar multiple \(\alpha \odot_T v_{\gamma, p}\) according to the operational definition of scalar multiplication in the tangent space \(T_p\mathcal{M}\).
